rationale: Both involve GSH (glutathione) but depletion describes loss of GSH while conjugation describes a chemical reaction using GSH — same object, different processes.
Both describe increased fat mass using nearly identical wording.
Increased lipid accumulation and increased lipid droplets describe the same cellular process of lipid storage accumulation.
Both describe adipocyte changes contributing to obesity but one specifies increased size and the other increased numbers — same object, different biological processes at the cellular level.
Decreased oligodendrocyte differentiation and impaired oligodendrocyte maturation describe the same biological process of oligodendrocyte developmental failure.
Hypomyelination is the cellular/molecular process while altered white brain matter is the tissue-level manifestation in a specific brain compartment.
Increased demyelination and impaired axonal insulation both describe loss of the myelin sheath around axons.
IAV binding to sialic acid receptor and IAV cell entry share the same virus-host interface but binding and entry are distinct sequential processes.
IAV production and IAV budding both describe viral replication output but production is broader while budding is the specific egress process.
Vascular endothelial dysfunction and vascular disrupting effects both describe dysfunction/disruption of the vascular endothelium.
Disturbed radial glia cell alignment/migration and decreased radial glia cell density describe related but distinct aspects of radial glia pathology.

These events all involve laminin but describe distinct processes: extracellular matrix laminin binding, disrupted integrin-laminin receptor binding, and decreased neural progenitor cell adhesion to laminin.
Plasma estradiol increased and estradiol availability increased both describe elevated estradiol levels in plasma/systemic availability.
Aromatase induction describes increased aromatase activity while inhibition of aromatase activity in plasma describes the opposite direction on the same enzyme.

These events all involve PPAR isoforms but describe distinct processes: stressor binding, disrupted nuclear signaling, dysregulation of transcriptional expression, and activation — same object, different processes.
Cardiac remodelling and abnormal cardiac structure and function both describe pathological changes to heart structure and function.
Increased delay in heart electrical conduction and altered cardiac electrical conduction both describe the same pathological change in cardiac conduction.
Increased early premature depolarizations during repolarization and increased delayed and early afterdepolarizations describe overlapping cardiac electrophysiological disturbances.
Ryanodine receptor activation and hyperphosphorylation of RyR2 both target the ryanodine receptor but through distinct processes (functional activation vs. post-translational modification).
Increased incidence of respiratory disease and dysfunction of respiratory system both describe adverse respiratory outcomes at the organ/system level.
Increased bone remodeling and occurrence of bone loss share the same biological object (bone) but remodeling is a process while bone loss is an outcome — distinct processes requiring curator review.
Reduction of fetal/adult testosterone and decreased insulin-like peptide 3 (INSL3) both relate to testicular endocrine function but measure different hormones produced by Leydig cells.
Disruption of estrogen receptor and estrogen receptor alpha inactivation both describe loss of estrogen receptor function, with the latter being more specific to ERα.
Increase in pro-inflammatory mediators and increased pro-inflammatory cytokine expression both describe elevated inflammatory signaling molecules.
Disrupted spermatogenesis and sperm quality and increased histomorphological alteration of testis both describe testicular pathology but at different levels — functional vs. morphological.
Impaired blood-testis barrier and depletion of ectoplasmic specialization describe related but distinct structures — ectoplasmic specializations are part of the BTB architecture.
Decreased sodium uptake in gills and decreased plasma sodium concentrations describe the same ionic imbalance at different biological levels (organ vs. systemic).
Disrupted TCA cycle and disrupted energy metabolism both describe impairment of core mitochondrial/cellular energy production processes.

Increased SREBP2 expression, increased cholesterol synthesis enzymes, and increased plasma LDL cholesterol describe sequential steps in the same cholesterol synthesis pathway at different biological levels.

Increase in androgen receptor protein expression/abundance and increased androgen receptor activation describe the same receptor but through different processes (expression level vs. functional activation).

Generation of gluten-reactive T cell receptors and generation of gluten-reactive and transglutaminase 2 reactive B cell receptors both describe antigen-specific receptor generation in celiac disease context, though involving different lymphocyte types.
Gluten-reactive CD4+ T cell activation and co-localization of gluten-reactive adaptive T cells with antigen presenting cells describe related but distinct events in gluten-specific T cell responses.
Activation of MEK/ERK1/2 and activation of MAPK describe the same mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling cascade.
Increased LMNA mutation and structural changes in lamin A/C both involve lamin A/C but mutation is a genetic event while structural changes are a protein-level consequence.
Increased intracellular copper and increased cuproptosis describe cause and distinct biological outcome of copper toxicity — related but not synonymous processes.
Decreased DNA methylation of FAM50B/PTCHD3 and elevated gene expression of FAM50B/PTCHD3 involve the same gene locus but describe an epigenetic modification vs. a transcriptional outcome.

Redox cycling by mitochondria and elevated mitochondrial ROS and dysfunction describe related mitochondrial processes — redox cycling is a mechanism that can generate ROS, but they are distinct events.
Activation of oxidative stress pathway and altered redox homeostasis both describe disruption of the cellular oxidative stress/redox balance.
Increased lysolecithin and increased lysolecithin cell membrane integration describe the same molecule at different stages — systemic increase vs. membrane-level integration.
Prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia and prostate cancer describe progressive stages of the same pathological process in the same organ.
Increased cardiac fibrosis and increased cardiac remodeling both describe structural cardiac pathology but fibrosis is a specific ECM process while remodeling is broader.
HCN channel inhibition and reduced pacemaker activity in the SA node describe the same functional consequence at different levels — molecular channel vs. tissue-level pacemaker output.
Slowed heart rate and reduced pacemaker activity in SA node both describe decreased cardiac rate but at different biological scales — systemic output vs. nodal mechanism.
Steroidogenesis dysregulation and granulosa cell damage both describe ovarian pathology but one is a functional/biochemical process and the other is a cellular injury event.
Innate immune response activation and microglia activation both describe innate immune activation, though microglia activation is CNS-specific — grouping for curator review.
Decreased Bcl-2 expression (anti-apoptotic) and increased Bax expression (pro-apoptotic) are directionally opposite changes in apoptosis-regulating proteins that together promote apoptosis.

Increased estradiol to progesterone ratio (estrogen dominance) and reduction of 17β-estradiol/11-keto testosterone ratio both describe altered sex hormone ratios but in different species/hormonal contexts.
Hypospadias and impaired urethral tube closure describe the same developmental defect at different levels of description — outcome vs. developmental process.
